text: The engines. Four of them. We didn't build them. She sold them to us. The valve plates are in a language that isn't a language.
The flight plan. The Atlantic. And a last waypoint in a desert nobody here had heard of. I asked who wrote it. Nobody wrote it.
The crew list. Crew: provided. I asked, provided by whom. They said it was handled. I resigned that afternoon. Nobody accepted it.
That... that was Beck. The night crane. He wouldn't leave the hangar either.
There she is. Der Kranich. The most beautiful thing I have ever made. I would give anything for her never to fly.
Is that... are there people on the line? This is Wittkamp. I'm in the tunnel office. I can see you on the canteen camera. Don't... the doors lock from my side. I locked them. I'm sorry.
You've turned the lights on. Thank you. I've been in the dark for six days with a model aeroplane.
The impellers are turning over. I didn't start them. If you go in there... if you go in there, cut the fuel lines in the port room. Please. It's the only thing I ask.
You've got my line. Listen. The hangar door is a key and a code. The code is the wing's weight in kilos. It's in the tunnel log. Jette wrote it. Then she wrote no.
If anyone is hearing this aboard, I'm sorry. The autopilot takes a key and both hands. It was never meant to take a crew.
Anselm, if you're still in there. It was never a test. I should have told you.
